$comment: What the clean command treats as left over from tooling a workspace no longer uses. Every entry is evidence of a retired installer or framework layout, not a guess: the AI-Assisted Work, Architecture and Research frameworks were once cloned into a workspace as submodules and installed by their own commands, which wrote the modules block of .aaw-config.yaml and the aaw-*, aar-* and research-dag skills that the work, research and literature-discovery skills replaced. A retired name the lock still installs is left alone: the repository pins a release that has it. Add an entry here, with the release that retired it, rather than widening a rule in code.

submodules.why: the AI-Assisted Work framework clone, retired when AAW 4.0.0 shipped standalone skills
the AI-Assisted Architecture framework clone, retired for the skills.mjs installer
the AI-Assisted Research framework clone, retired when AAR 2.0.0 shipped standalone skills

skills.why: an AI-Assisted Work skill from before 4.0.0, replaced by the work skill
an AI-Assisted Research skill from before 2.0.0, replaced by the research skill
replaced by the research skill in AI-Assisted Research 2.0.0
an AI-Assisted Architecture skill folded into the architecture skill, whose flows replace it
folded into the architecture skill's stage flow, formerly its rung flow
folded into the architecture skill's check flow

configBlocks.why: the module table the framework installers wrote; nothing reads it since the standalone skills, and the rest of the file (the thread store) stays

generated.why: Docusaurus's cache, rebuilt by the next build
the last site build, rebuilt by the next build

hookPatterns.why: runs a framework installer that no longer exists
reads a framework clone that clean removes
